feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed. Integration compensation: I kept the iteration 5 controller exactly (kp 3.5, kd 0.5, ki 0.05, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), so the spread change is isolated. The weights are index-based, so the 0.0225 m pitch keeps the same gradient and no rescaling is needed. Evidence: iteration 5 (score 422.9) has the best oval finish (95%) and slalom line losses of 1.85. Iteration 2 showed that 16 mm sensors at y=0.07 m helped, iteration 1 showed that spread alone at y=0.04 m did not, and iteration 3 showed that y=0.08 m with seven sensors raised oscillation and cut the oval finish rate to 35%. Depending on the next race: if slalom line_loss_events drop below 1.85 and the oval finish stays at or above 90%, keep ±0.045 m, since the outer coverage was the slalom limit. If the oval finish falls below 90% and slalom does not improve, the spread is adding steering lag, so revert to ±0.036 m and stop widening. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 while max_error does not move, the gain is the limit, and I will retune kd on my side rather than change geometry.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.85 and the oval finish rate stays at or above 90%, keep ±0.045 m at y=0.07 m with 16 mm footprints and try x = ±0.050 m (0.025 m pitch). Iteration 2 showed that look-ahead with 16 mm sensors gave the first real gain, and this extends the same coverage logic outward.

If the oval finish rate falls below 90% while slalom line losses do not improve, revert the outer sensors to ±0.036 m (iteration 5 layout) and raise wheel_radius from 0.040 to 0.045 m. Iteration 4 showed that radius lifted the oval finish rate from 65% to 80%, so speed is the cheaper fix than more spread.

Keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and mass at 0.5 kg for this step. Iteration 6 showed 0.4 kg lowered s-bend progress (0.72 to 0.59), and iteration 7 showed 0.09 m track hurt the oval finish rate (95% to 60%).
